text.title: Spring Boot Layered Architecture Failure Modes
text.summary: 10 antipatterns observed in real Spring Boot 3 codebases. Each pairs symptom + root cause + concrete fix.

antipattern.symptom: Endpoint returns Hibernate proxy fields or throws `LazyInitializationException`; agent papers over with `@JsonIgnore` on the entity.
antipattern.root-cause: Controller returns entity instead of DTO.
antipattern.fix: Define a Java record DTO; map via MapStruct in the service layer; remove `@JsonIgnore` from the entity.

antipattern.symptom: Multi-step write succeeds partially after a runtime exception; downstream invariants broken; database in inconsistent state.
antipattern.root-cause: Service write method missing `@Transactional`; each JDBC call auto-commits.
antipattern.fix: Annotate every write method `@Transactional`. Add a class-level `@Transactional(readOnly = true)` default; let writes override.

antipattern.symptom: Endpoint times out as table grows; profile shows full-table scan returning 5M rows.
antipattern.fix: Accept `Pageable` and return `Page<DTO>`; default size = 20. Reject list endpoints without `Pageable` in review.

antipattern.symptom: Mapper interface compiles but throws `InstantiationException` at runtime: `cannot instantiate interface UserMapper`.
antipattern.root-cause: `mapstruct-processor` annotation processor missing from `pom.xml` / `build.gradle`; no impl generated.
antipattern.fix: Configure the annotation processor explicitly; verify `target/generated-sources/annotations/.../UserMapperImpl.java` is produced.

antipattern.symptom: Boot 3 codebase compiles locally but throws `NoSuchMethodError` in CI: a transitive dep still uses `javax.persistence.Entity`.
antipattern.root-cause: Imports drifted; some files still on `javax.*` after the Jakarta migration.
antipattern.fix: Run `grep -r 'javax\.persistence\|javax\.validation' src/` in CI; fail the build on any hit. Migrate all imports.

antipattern.symptom: `@Transactional` method called from another method on `this`; transaction never starts; rollback never happens.
antipattern.root-cause: Self-invocation bypasses the proxy that wraps `@Transactional`.
antipattern.fix: Move the `@Transactional` method to a separate bean and inject it; or use `AopContext.currentProxy()` (with `exposeProxy=true`) as a last resort.

antipattern.symptom: `@Transactional` sits on a controller method. The DB transaction spans the whole HTTP request including JSON serialisation; lazy collections fire queries mid-response and row locks are held for the request duration.
antipattern.root-cause: The transaction boundary was placed on the wrong layer — usually to make a `LazyInitializationException` go away.
antipattern.fix: Move `@Transactional` to the service method per `transactional-on-service-only`. The controller calls the service and returns a DTO; nothing transactional lives in the HTTP layer.

antipattern.symptom: The controller autowires a repository and orchestrates two or three services; `@WebMvcTest` no longer covers it, so the endpoint is only reachable through a full `@SpringBootTest`.
antipattern.root-cause: Business logic accreted in the web layer because that was where the request already was.
antipattern.fix: Push the orchestration into one service method per `thin-controller`; the controller keeps a single service call. The logic then becomes reusable from a scheduler or a queue consumer.

antipattern.symptom: An `@Async` method such as `sendEmail()` is called via `this.sendEmail(...)` from another method of the same bean. It runs synchronously; the observed thread is the request thread.
antipattern.root-cause: Self-invocation never crosses the proxy, so `@Async` is never applied.
antipattern.fix: Extract the `@Async` methods into a separate bean, inject it, and call `emailSender.sendEmail(...)`. Define a named executor bean and annotate `@Async("emailExecutor")` per `async-via-named-executor`.

antipattern.symptom: Controllers return a bespoke `ApiErrorResponse{code, message, timestamp, ...}`. Each new endpoint duplicates the envelope and every client writes its own parser.
antipattern.root-cause: A custom error shape was rolled by hand instead of using the standard `ProblemDetail`.
antipattern.fix: Replace with a single `@RestControllerAdvice` mapping domain exceptions to `ProblemDetail` (RFC 7807). One error format across every endpoint, and OpenAPI generation describes it for free.
